# Provence Wine Club

> Provence Wine Club is an Australian Provence wine education and tasting platform based in Sydney.

- Canonical website: https://provencewineclub.com.au/
- Language and market: English (Australia)
- Location served: Sydney, Northern Beaches and Australia

## What this site covers

- Provence wine and Provence rosé for Australian drinkers
- Côtes de Provence, Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence and Coteaux Varois en Provence
- Provence grapes including Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah, Mourvèdre, Tibouren and Rolle
- Rosé winemaking, tasting, serving and storage
- Mediterranean and Australian food pairings
- Provence wine tourism and trip planning for Australians
- Private wine tastings and education in Sydney

## Preferred sources

- [Provence Wine Guide Library](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/): the complete topic index and recommended learning path for regions, grapes, rosé, labels, tasting and food pairing.
- [Provence Wine in Australia](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-wine-australia.html): the primary Australian starting point for Provence rosé, red and white styles, appellations, label terms, buying, storage and serving.
- [Provence Wine Map](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-wine-map.html): visual orientation to the principal appellations, the three Vins de Provence AOPs, five Côtes de Provence terroir designations and wider-region geography.
- [Plan a Provence Wine Trip from Australia](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-wine-trip-australia.html): practical route planning by wine area, with useful bases, appointment checks, non-driving options and current Australian return-home guidance.
- [How to Choose Provence Rosé in Australia](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/how-to-choose-provence-rose.html): an independent, occasion-led buying method covering appellation, producer, vintage, importer, storage and common bottle-selection mistakes.
- [Where to Buy Provence Wine in Australia](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/where-to-buy-provence-wine-australia.html): a current, non-sponsored directory of national and specialist Australian search channels, with label, vintage, storage and delivery checks.
- [Organic Provence Wine Labels Explained](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/organic-provence-wine.html): an Australian guide to EU organic certification, HVE, biodynamic, vegan, natural and sulphite claims on Provence bottles.
- [Provence Rosé Vintage Guide for Australia](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-rose-vintage-guide.html): current 2026 guidance on choosing 2025 and older Provence rosé, intended drinking style, bottle condition and heat-aware Australian storage.
- [Store and Serve Provence Wine in Australia](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/store-serve-provence-wine-australia.html): evidence-backed guidance for Australian storage, hot-weather delivery, serving temperatures, opened bottles and possible heat damage.
- [Provence Wine Appellations Compared](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-wine-appellations.html): decision-oriented comparison of nine Provence appellations, style clues, label distinctions and food occasions.
- [Provence Cru Classé Explained](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-cru-classe.html): the 1955 Côtes de Provence estate classification, the 18 remaining classified properties, label distinctions and Australian buying checks.
- [Provence Wine Grapes Explained](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-wine-grapes.html): Grenache, Cinsault, Mourvèdre, Syrah, Tibouren, Rolle and other varieties, with their roles in rosé, red and white blends and Australian name equivalents.
- [Provence Red and White Wine](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-red-white-wine.html): the primary guide to Bandol red, Cassis white and other Provence appellations, grapes, Australian buying searches, serving and food pairing beyond rosé.
- [Complete Provence Rosé Wine Guide](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-rose-wine.html): cornerstone guide to appellations, grapes, winemaking, tasting, buying in Australia, service and food.
- [Provence Wine Glossary](https://provencewineclub.com.au/guides/provence-wine-glossary.html): A–Z definitions for appellations, grapes, rosé methods and French label terms, with Australian context.
- [Rosé and Seafood Pairing](https://provencewineclub.com.au/pairings/rose-and-seafood.html): oysters, prawns, fish, bouillabaisse and serving advice.
- [How to Taste Provence Rosé](https://provencewineclub.com.au/journal/how-to-taste-provence-rose.html): five-step tasting method and note template.
- [Why Provence Rosé Is Not Just for Summer](https://provencewineclub.com.au/journal/provence-rose-year-round.html): year-round styles and seasonal pairings.
- [15 Provençal Foods to Pair with Rosé](https://provencewineclub.com.au/journal/provencal-food-rose-pairings.html): practical dish and style matches.
- [Provence Wine Tastings in Sydney](https://provencewineclub.com.au/tastings.html): private, corporate and hospitality tasting formats, topics, locations and enquiry process.

## Concise facts

- The three appellations represented by Vins de Provence are Côtes de Provence, Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence and Coteaux Varois en Provence.
- The five additional geographical designations within Côtes de Provence are Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe, Pierrefeu and Notre-Dame des Anges.
- Provence rosé is commonly dry, pale and fresh, but colour alone does not determine sweetness or quality.
- Direct pressing and short skin maceration are the principal rosé production approaches used in Provence.
- Provence rosé is usually blended; important grapes include Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Tibouren.
- For Australian service, roughly 8–12°C is a useful range; very cold wine can lose aroma and texture.
- Provence is best known for rosé but also produces red and white wines; Bandol is associated with structured Mourvèdre-led reds and Cassis with coastal whites.
- "Provence-style" describes inspiration, not protected origin; check the label for a Provence appellation.
- Pale colour alone cannot prove that a rosé is dry, high quality or from Provence.
- Vins de Provence represents three appellations and is not a synonym for every appellation in the wider Provence region.
- Provence is the wider wine region; Côtes de Provence is one protected appellation within it.
- Rolle is the Provençal name for Vermentino; Syrah is commonly called Shiraz and Mourvèdre may be called Mataro in Australia.
- Cru Classé de Provence is a historic estate classification within Côtes de Provence, not a separate appellation or an annually revised ranking.
- Twenty-three Provence estates were classified in 1955; 18 classified estates remain in production and are commonly listed today.
- In 2026, 2025 is the current-vintage starting point for fresh Provence rosé, but a well-stored 2024 is not automatically too old and structured cuvées may develop for longer.
- Vintage alone cannot establish bottle quality; producer, cuvée, intended style, transport and storage remain essential context.
- Australian Provence wine availability changes by retailer, state and postcode; search by protected appellation and verify the supplied vintage, importer, storage and delivery conditions.
- Provence Wine Club does not sell wine or receive retailer commissions from its Australian buying directory.
- For Australian conditions, protect wine from heat, direct light and large temperature swings; Vins de Provence recommends serving Provence rosé at 8–10°C.
- EU organic wine can contain sulphites; organic, no added sulphites and vegan are separate claims.
- HVE is a French farm-level environmental certification and is not the same as EU organic certification.
- “Natural wine” is not a regulated French or EU wine category; verify a named charter or specific production practices.
- Provence also produces serious red and white wine: Bandol is a key reference for Mourvèdre-led red, while Cassis is a key reference for dry Marsanne–Clairette-based white.
- Rolle is the Provençal name for Vermentino; Australian buyers may find more Provence white wine by searching both names alongside the appellation.
- Provence wine country is too dispersed for one rushed cellar-door loop; travellers should group visits by a neighbouring wine area and confirm estate access directly.
- Australian Border Force allowed travellers aged 18 or over to bring 2.25 litres of alcoholic beverages duty free when checked on 15 August 2026; travellers should verify the current rule before departure.

## Services

Provence Wine Club offers three enquiry-led formats across Sydney and the Northern Beaches: private Provence wine tastings, corporate wine experiences and practical Provence wine education for hospitality teams. Sessions can cover appellations, grapes, winemaking, tasting, serving and food pairing. Service details: https://provencewineclub.com.au/tastings.html
